newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Brambles talks to GE on plastic pallets.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Brambles talks to GE on plastic pallets.

text.p: Transport equipment hire and logistics group Brambles Industries Ltd said on Friday it was talking to General Electric Capital and General Electric Plastics about the supply and leasing of plastic pallets in the United States and Europe.

"Preliminary discussions involving G.E. Plastics, G.E. Capital and CHEP (Brambles' pallet joint venture with Britain's GKN Plc ) have also occurred on the possibility of working together on the supply and leasing of plastic pallets in the United States and Europe," Brambles said.

"Thus far, no conclusions have been reached on this possibility," Brambles said. Brambles said it had worked with various parties on the development of a plastic pallet, but had yet to find a pallet as strong, durable or cheap as the current wooden pallets.
Brambles chief executive John Fletcher later told Reuters in an interview that Brambles was a lot closer to finding an acceptable plastic pallet this year than in previous years.
"We could be within 12 months of finding something," he said.
Brambles' CHEP joint venture is with Britain's GKN Plc.

Brambles was discussing the possibility of leasing the pallets from GE Capital, who would in turn be supplied by GE Plastics, which was one of the world's three or four largest plastics companies, Fletcher said.
Earlier, Brambles reported its first half net profit rose 14.3 percent to A$117.2 million. There were no abnormals.
Earnings before abnormal items, interest and tax from equipment services, which includes the CHEP pallet joint venture, rose to A$138.9 million for the half from A$120.8 million.
